narrative:
**Week of 2026-09-28 — Hugging Face developer activity**

Downloads and likes moved in opposite directions this week. Model downloads rose 20.6% to 3.43M across the 25,492 models tracked, while engagement signals fell sharply: model likes dropped 27.9% to 8,541 and Space likes nearly halved, down 48.5% to 610. On the supply side, catalog growth was concentrated outside the headline families — "other-open" models rose 36.7% to 7,909, Gemma rose 57.8% to 819, and Llama rose 25.6% to 1,297, while Qwen slipped 6.6% to 5,557 and Mistral fell 30.7% to 167. Kimi/Moonshot dropped from 54 to 22 models; the week-over-week percentage is reportable against the 25,492-model base but is driven by a very small count and should not be read as a trend.

Across the 6,522 Spaces (full coverage for the use-case cut), education was the standout mover, up 35.3% to 249 Spaces, with the education vertical penetration rising 16.1% to 8.72% and healthcare up 34.9% to 4.78%. Coding Spaces fell 16.4% to 255, music generation fell 34.6% to 51, and robotics fell 20% to 44 — the latter two off bases small enough that the direction matters more than the magnitude. Chat-assistant remained the largest named category at 999 Spaces (-4.6%), and "other" held roughly steady at 1,903 (-0.03%). On tooling, static Spaces grew 4.0% to 3,715 and Gradio eased 1.9% to 2,167, with Docker up 2.6% to 507 and Streamlit down 13.5% to 64. Technology tags showed a shift away from agent-style builds (agentic 6.18%, -15.0%; tool-use 3.65%, -16.6%) toward customization and retrieval (fine-tuned 3.85%, +39.9%; RAG 2.61%, +25.4%; speech 3.24%, +15.7%); vision-language remained the most penetrated tag at 7.79% (+7.9%).

Within use cases, Qwen held the top share of coding Spaces at 39.1% of 156 (+14.2%) as proprietary-API share there fell 57.3% to 4.5%, while in chat-assistant Qwen share declined 16.2% to 22.6% and proprietary-API rose 23.7% to 13.0%. Two methodology caveats: 9,356 models (36.7% of the catalog) are still unclassified as "unknown" family, which caps the reliability of family-share readings; and several use-case denominators are very small — robotics (18), music generation (26), education (36) and 3D/gaming (37) — so sub-family shifts in those cuts are too few to report meaningfully. No 4-week or 12-week deltas were available, so all comparisons here are single-week. Next week, watch whether the download surge is sustained or whether the fall in likes signals a genuine cooling in developer engagement rather than a one-week data artifact.
